prompt.context: FormCo is the leading manufacturer of paper-based business forms. The majority of FormCo's products are sold through banks to small businesses and consumers. Increases in paperless and online transactions have decreased demand for FormCo's main products. When FormCo's products are sold through the banks, customers rarely choose higher-margin, premium products. FormCo wants to develop a phone-based direct-to-customer channel to encourage customers to order directly, rather than through banks, and to increase the probability of upselling higher-margin products.
prompt.question: Should FormCo pursue its proposed idea of developing the phone-based direct-to-customer channel?

clarifying_info.q: Can you explain the difference between the two channels?
clarifying_info.a: Bank channel: Banks offer FormCo products to their existing customers without additional sales/marketing effort. If interested, customers place orders with the bank but sometimes call FormCo's call centers for simple inquiries. Direct-to-Customer channel: Customers call directly to inquire and place orders. Call center representatives must have more specialized knowledge to handle this channel.

exhibits.title: 2004 Projected Orders and Revenue
exhibits.shows: Two side-by-side bar charts comparing 2003 actuals vs. 2004 projected figures for the Banks channel and the Direct-to-Customers channel

exhibits.title: Call Center Volume
exhibits.shows: Stacked bar chart showing daily call volumes by call type (Customer Service, Bank Orders, Direct to Customer, Other) for four call centers (Phoenix, Dallas, Charlotte, Salt Lake City), along with each center's total call capacity

framework: Assess incremental revenue from the new direct-to-customer channel: new customers and higher-margin upsells
Assess cannibalization: estimate how much of the bank channel revenue loss is caused by the new channel vs. secular demand decline
Assess incremental costs: call center setup/expansion, incremental labor (specialty reps), and SG&A
Calculate net incremental profit to determine if the channel is financially viable
If profitable, evaluate execution risks: operational impact, learning curve, competitive reaction
If not profitable, explore alternative strategies to improve FormCo's profitability

questions.prompt: What conclusions can you draw from Exhibit 1 about the proposed direct-to-customer channel?
questions.guidance: Candidate should observe: (1) The Direct-to-Customers channel generates higher revenue per order ($1,000M / 80M orders = $12.50/order) vs. the Banks channel ($600M / 120M orders = $5.00/order). (2) The Banks channel loses both volume (210M to 120M orders) and revenue ($1,100M to $600M). Candidate should flag cannibalization as a key issue.

math.setup: Revenue per order comparison: Direct channel = $1,000M / 80M orders; Banks channel (projected) = $600M / 120M orders
math.answer: Direct-to-customer channel generates $12.50/order vs. $5.00/order in the bank channel; bank revenue declines by $500M

questions.prompt: Calculate total incremental revenue from the new direct-to-customer channel, accounting for cannibalization.
questions.guidance: 80% of the bank channel revenue loss ($500M) is due to cannibalization by the new channel. Incremental revenue = new channel revenue minus cannibalized bank revenue.

math.setup: Incremental revenue = Direct channel revenue - (cannibalization rate x Bank channel revenue loss)

questions.prompt: Given per-order costs (COGS $2.3, other costs $5.0), calculate incremental profit per order and total annual incremental profit.
questions.guidance: Candidate should calculate incremental revenue per order using total incremental revenue divided by the new channel order volume, then subtract per-order costs to get incremental profit per order, and multiply by order volume for total annual profit.

math.setup: Incremental revenue per order = Incremental revenue / Orders; Incremental profit per order = Revenue per order - COGS per order - Other costs per order
steps: Total annual incremental profit = $0.20 x 80M orders = $16M
math.answer: Incremental profit per order = $0.20; Total annual incremental profit = $16M

questions.prompt: FormCo implemented the direct-to-customer channel but did not achieve projected profit. Orders and revenue are as projected; overall costs are higher than expected. What might explain this?
questions.guidance: Candidate should structure the diagnosis across both revenue and cost dimensions. Since the interviewer confirms revenue is on track, the candidate should focus on cost drivers: higher-than-expected labor costs, process inefficiencies, call routing issues, higher raw material costs, etc.

questions.prompt: Using Exhibit 2, what conclusions can you draw about the call centers?
questions.guidance: (1) All call centers are underutilized — Phoenix has the lowest utilization (1,295/1,400 = 92%; but other centers show more slack). Opportunity to consolidate call centers to reduce costs. (2) Only Phoenix and Dallas handle direct-to-customer calls; Charlotte and Salt Lake City handle none. This may reflect an intentional routing strategy or a constraint that only those two centers can handle the new channel.

math.setup: Utilization = total daily calls / call capacity for each center
math.answer: All centers are underutilized; consolidation opportunity exists. Phoenix and Dallas are the only centers handling direct-to-customer calls.

questions.prompt: For the Phoenix call center, total annual cost of the new channel is $313M. COGS is 30%, call center rep salary is 55% (Regular reps 15%, Specialty reps 40%), and other costs are 15%. Phoenix handles 53% of new channel calls (assume proportional to orders and revenue). Calculate Phoenix's annual revenue and profit from the new channel.
questions.guidance: Candidate should calculate Phoenix revenue as 53% of total incremental revenue ($600M), then subtract Phoenix's share of total new channel costs ($313M) to get profit. Note: the $313M represents total new channel cost, so Phoenix's cost must be computed appropriately. The casebook states Phoenix revenue = $320M and profit = $7M, implying Phoenix's cost = $313M (i.e., $313M is the Phoenix call center's own cost, not the total across all centers).

math.setup: Phoenix revenue = 53% x total incremental revenue; Phoenix profit = Phoenix revenue - Phoenix annual cost
steps: Phoenix rep salary = 55% x $313M = $172M (Specialty reps = 40% x $313M = $125M; Regular reps = 15% x $313M = $47M)
math.answer: Phoenix annual revenue ≈ $320M; Phoenix annual profit = $7M

brainstorming.prompt: Based on the Phoenix call center cost structure, brainstorm ways to improve the cost structure and profitability of the direct-to-customer channel.

categories.name: Reduce Specialty Rep Costs (highest priority — 40% of total cost)
ideas: Analyze all incoming direct-to-customer inquiries to identify which ones are simple enough to be routed to Regular reps instead of Specialty reps
Standardize answers to common inquiries and allow Regular reps or an automated phone system (IVR) to handle them
Create an FAQ on the internet or via automated phone prompts to deflect simple calls entirely

categories.name: Fix Call Routing
ideas: Implement a better routing system to ensure bank channel customers are not mis-routed to Specialty reps
Use call classification logic to triage calls before they reach a rep

categories.name: Call Center Consolidation
ideas: Consolidate underutilized call centers to reduce fixed overhead
Particularly focus on Salt Lake City which is at only 48% utilization

categories.name: Workforce Management
ideas: Right-size staffing levels to match actual call volumes
Cross-train Regular reps to handle a broader set of inquiry types

recommendation: The direct-to-customer channel is financially viable — it generates $16M in annual incremental profit — so FormCo should pursue it
However, the channel is currently underperforming due to higher-than-expected costs, primarily driven by over-reliance on Specialty reps for all direct-to-customer inquiries
risks: Cannibalization risk: 80% of bank channel decline is attributed to the new channel, which limits net incremental gain
Cost overrun risk: Specialty rep labor costs (40% of total) are disproportionately high and will continue to suppress profit if not addressed
Execution risk: Call routing inefficiencies and underutilized centers may persist without deliberate process redesign
next_steps: Conduct inquiry analysis to categorize direct-to-customer calls by complexity and reroute simpler calls to Regular reps or automated systems
Implement improved call routing logic to prevent bank channel calls from reaching Specialty reps
Evaluate call center consolidation, especially Salt Lake City, to reduce fixed cost overhead
Track upsell rates and premium product mix to confirm the channel is achieving its strategic goal
